judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of Code-based instrument categories; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 and Borrower Collateral clause (i) use the term identically.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(less portions that are not in compliance with the definition thereof)" is circular, since ineligible portions are already excluded by the Eligible Notes Receivable definition itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Eligible Notes Receivable definition already contains its own "to the extent" portion-based exclusions (clauses (l), (p), (t), (u)), so this second netting step risks double-counting in the Borrowing Base.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is keyed to entities formed "after the Effective Date", a capitalised term that appears nowhere in the definitions or operative text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Everywhere else the agreement measures from the "Closing Date" — including the parallel carve-out in the Subsidiary definition, which uses "Closing Date" for the identical concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires the securing real property to be "owned by the maker of such note", a narrowing element easy to overlook and easy to fail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Neither the Eligible Notes Receivable list nor the Note Receivable Collateral definition repeats the maker-ownership requirement, so notes secured by third-party property fall outside the base definition though the eligibility machinery seems to contemplate them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The syntax ("in which Fund has a title-insured first priority lien, or security title to, that has been assigned or pledged to Lender") is broken, leaving unclear what must be assigned and what the antecedent of "that" is.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition is limited to property securing an *Eligible* Note Receivable, yet Sections 4.9(c), 6.3(e) and Permitted Dispositions clause (f) speak of Note Receivable Collateral in the context of defaulted and foreclosed notes, which by definition are not eligible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An all-embracing definition; the inclusion of "covenants" and "duties" as "Obligations" makes the payment-in-full concept less crisp than it looks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.4's final sentence and Section 3.6 both address what repayment in full means, and many sections carve out Bank Product Obligations; the pieces fit but require careful reconciliation, and the term drives the Senior Leverage Ratio covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]nd related agreements and instruments" is an open catch-all appended to three specific documents, and the defined term is used as though it were a single document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 5.3, 5.8 and 6.3(d)(iii) treat the Offering Circular as one document that can be "made available" or "filed", which sits awkwardly with a collective definition including the operating agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined entirely by reference to a form to be "submitted by Lender" with responses "satisfactory to Lender"; content is wholly extrinsic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b)(vi) requires its delivery as a condition precedent and it is a Loan Document; consistent, if unspecified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4 defines Overadvance as cross-referenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(d) defines Participant as cross-referenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[R]easonable (from the perspective of a secured asset-based lender) business judgment" is a deliberately elastic standard, and it governs many of Lender's most consequential unilateral powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside other, different standards in the same instrument — "sole discretion" (Borrower's Required Procedures, Section 3.1(k)), "reasonable judgment", and unqualified "deems" in the Defaulted Note Receivable definition — an unharmonised patchwork.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed seven-item list with quantified conditions in clause (e); expressio unius arguments are possible but the list is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 4.1, 7.3(c) and 7.4 all permit only Permitted Dispositions, and Section 4.9(b) releases Liens on a sale "in accordance with the terms of this Agreement"; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of four named individuals; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Change of Control definition requires Permitted Holders to own 100% of Manager and of Servicer, while Stephanie Ng Kelly is an Executive Officer and Validity Agreement Party but not a Permitted Holder — a slight but real asymmetry.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six enumerated categories, each tied to the ordinary course or to identified events; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.12 permits only these, and clause (d) preserves the Borrowers' core lending business; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (c)'s proviso is ungrammatical — "so long as such Liens for Approved Debt or subordinated to the Liens held by Lender" omits a verb, leaving the condition on Approved Debt Liens unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens contemplates Liens securing Approved Debt while "Subordinated Debt" is defined as *unsecured* Indebtedness and "Subordinated Note" is expressly "secured by the assets of Fund" — the three cannot all be right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Condition (c) turns on whether "Lender is satisfied", an unqualified subjective test, though (a) and (b) are objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 6.7, 6.11 and 3.1(i) all rely on Permitted Protests consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single hard dollar cap; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1(c) permits it and Permitted Liens clause (e) secures it; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole concept is anchored to a "written description provided to Lender by Borrowers prior to the Closing Date" that is not attached, and to open-ended "other actions and undertakings incidental thereto".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly contemplates admitting Manager and Servicer as managing members, which on its face can trigger the Change of Control definition prohibited by Section 7.8, and it is carved out of Sections 7.3, 7.6 and 7.12 without those carve-outs being reconciled with Section 7.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but conventional enumeration; nothing contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used ubiquitously without variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes required content precisely; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Projections" is defined but is not called for by Section 6.3 or any other operative covenant, making it an orphan definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 20-day acquisition-financing test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Permitted Purchase Money Indebtedness, Section 7.1(c) and Permitted Liens clause (e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]r other similar process in which a Borrower took legal title" is a modest catch-all after two specific routes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Permitted Dispositions (g), Permitted Investments (f) and the Borrowing Base Certificate definition consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and comprehensive; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Real Property is not an enumerated item of Borrower Collateral (it appears only in the proceeds tail), yet Section 2.13(h) waives defences "because the Obligations are secured by Real Property" — a mismatch worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the Code formulation; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.4's final passage makes a Record satisfy any writing requirement, consistently with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a)'s "or in any way address" and clause (e)'s residual are broad catch-alls after specific verbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Sections 6.13(c), 11.3(c) and the Lender Expenses definition consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A regulatory formula with an express zero default; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds the LIBOR Rate definition; consistent with Section 2.11's capital-adequacy mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clauses (d) and (e) are circular — a payment counts as a Restricted Payment only "to the extent such action would cause an Event of Default" or if "not expressly authorized in this Agreement", while the Event of Default arises from making a Restricted Payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.10 prohibits Restricted Payments subject to carve-outs that themselves authorise Tax Distributions and Subordinated Debt payments, so the circularity is completed by the operative covenant rather than resolved by it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line, purely arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(c) tests Revolver Usage against the Maximum Revolver Amount while Section 2.4 defines Overadvance by reference to "Obligations"; slightly different measures for related limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivial definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the Stock definition and Section 6.3(d); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporates the Code term; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.7 and 5.18 and the Control Agreement definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean two-element ratio; the words themselves are not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.16(b) caps this ratio, "expressed as a percentage", at 0.9%, which with the $600,000,000 minimum Tangible Net Worth would cap Obligations near $5.4 million and make the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount and the 20% Borrowing Base unusable — a genuine internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a single entity; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subsidiary definition expressly excludes Bar-K, Inc., and Sections 4.8 and 8.15 assume Servicer's role; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A] Servicing and Management Agreement" is indefinite — no date, no parties beyond a generic "Borrower", and no identification of which of the two Borrowers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b)(iv) makes it a condition precedent, Section 8.15 makes breach an Event of Default and Section 9.1(e)/(o) let Lender terminate or assume it, so an unidentified instrument carries substantial operative weight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific class plus "any settlement agent" covered by a Closing Protection Letter; the parenthetical list is illustrative but the covering-letter condition bounds it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.2(b), 3.1(t)(iv) and 6.18 use Settlement Agents consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare balance-sheet test ("assets greater than debts") that omits the customary capital-adequacy and ability-to-pay prongs, so "Solvent" here does not mean what it usually means.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.12 pairs it with a fraudulent-transfer representation whose statutory context assumes the fuller test, and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (q) applies it to makers; the narrow definition sits oddly there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated with an SEC-rule backstop; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes Investor Membership Interests "Stock", which is what makes Restricted Payments and Change of Control operate; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a) requires the debt to be "unsecured", a hard requirement stated in one word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subordinated Note definition describes notes evidencing Approved Debt as "secured by the assets of Fund", and Permitted Liens clause (c) contemplates Liens for Approved Debt — irreconcilable with clause (a)'s unsecured requirement once Approved Debt is folded in by clause (b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap formula is intricate and turns partly on amounts computed "in Manager's discretion", which makes the ceiling elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the notes are "secured by the assets of Fund", directly against the "unsecured" requirement in the Subordinated Debt definition and against Section 7.2's Lien covenant except as saved by Permitted Liens clause (c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clearly delineated cases with a satisfaction standard; determinate in function.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Referenced by the Subordinated Debt, Approved Debt and Permitted Reorganization definitions and Sections 7.7(b) and 7.10(b); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso excludes "any new corporation ... formed after the Closing Date" not funded with Borrower assets, which largely swallows the general definition for future entities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.13 forbids forming or acquiring "any Subsidiary" without consent, but the proviso means most newly formed entities are not Subsidiaries at all — the covenant and the definition pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the Code concept with an enumerated list of supported obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Borrower Collateral clause (j); no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula adds Subordinated Debt to members' equity and then deducts intangibles, prepaids and Affiliate receivables; unconventional but stated arithmetically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the denominator of the Senior Leverage Ratio and the subject of Section 7.16(a)'s $600,000,000 floor, whose interaction with the 0.9% ratio cap in 7.16(b) does not work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]axes, if any, payable by such holders (calculated at the highest applicable marginal rate)" mixes an actual-liability test with a hypothetical rate, and "such Borrower" has an uncertain antecedent after "Fund or Manager".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.10(a)(i) permits Tax Distributions when no Default exists; consistent in operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.5 does define Taxes as cross-referenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a) says merely that "an Event of Default has occurred", with no "and is continuing", so on its face a single cured default triggers the event forever.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(b) supplies "has occurred and is continuing" when using the term, which patches but does not eliminate the discrepancy between the definition and its only operative use.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivial definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition by reference to a satisfactory form; content is extrinsic but the function is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b)(iii) requires delivery and Section 8.12 makes termination a default; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of five named individuals; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.12 keys an Event of Default to these parties, and the list matches the Executive Officer list; consistent.
